title: Target classification and unique equivariant totally geodesic embedding for maximal complex hyperbolic lattice representations
difficulty_reason: After treating the already-counted cominuscule/foliated Milnor–Wood framework and mature KM17/Corlette results as given, the theorem still requires the exceptional E6(-14) half-spin model, its octonionic rank and kernel-intersection estimates, and their interaction with Higgs integrability to force vanishing of the antiholomorphic component. The authored closure integrates the tight SU(1,2)->SU(2,4)->E6 embedding, computes a compact centralizer and stabilizers, and proves uniqueness using CAT(0) convexity/sandwich and Borel density before removing covering and torsion restrictions.

source_disclosures: Every integer n>=2 and every uniform lattice Gamma subset SU(1,n), including lattices with torsion.
G_R=G(R)^0 for an algebraic group over R; G_R is semisimple with no compact factors and its noncompact symmetric space is Hermitian.
An arbitrary maximal representation rho:Gamma->G_R, with maximality |tau(rho)|=r_M vol(X) in the original normalizations.
No extra reductivity, simplicity of the target, torsion-free condition, or simply connected complexification condition.
Each simple factor is isogenous to SU(p,q), q>=np, or E6(-14). Exceptional E6(-14) factors can occur exactly when n=2.
The phrase 'the latter being possible if and only if n=2' modifies the exceptional possibility. For n=2, SU(p,q) factors and mixed semisimple targets remain allowed.
Positive Toledo gives rho-equivariant holomorphic f with f*omega_M=r_M omega; negative Toledo gives antiholomorphic f with f*omega_M=-r_M omega.
The same f is the unique rho-equivariant harmonic map, is a totally geodesic embedding, and is equivariant for a unique Lie group homomorphism phi:SU(1,n)->G_R.
Corollary B is not selected or counted. In particular no separate faithfulness/discreteness/compact-twist structure conclusion is appended to this theorem.
